content:
The image shows a soybean stem split lengthwise held up against the sky. Key observations:
- Stem interior (pith) appears **white/cream colored** — not brown
- The root system is **severely rotted/darkened/black** on the right side
- The lower stem/taproot junction shows dark discoloration
- Lateral roots appear dead and blackened

Key diagnostic clue: **white pith** differentiates SDS from Brown Stem Rot (which has brown pith). Let me check reference images for SDS, Brown Stem Rot, and Charcoal Rot.

Comparing the test image to references:
- **SDS reference** (bottom-left): shows darkened, rotted roots with possible bluish fungal growth — very similar to test image root system
- **Brown Stem Rot reference** (bottom-right): shows **brown/dark pith** inside split stem — test image pith is white/cream, NOT brown
- **Charcoal Rot reference** (top-left): shows stem held against sky, similar composition, but with gray charcoal-like interior

Let me view one more reference to confirm.

Looking at the Fusarium reference closely - the bottom panel shows split stems with **white pith and dark rotted roots**, very similar to the test image. Now comparing all candidates:

**Test image key features:**
- Stem split lengthwise showing **white/cream pith** (not brown)
- Root system is severely **dark/black and rotted**
- No external stem lesions above soil line
- Overall appearance of late-season systemic disease

**Assessment:**
- **Brown Stem Rot**: EXCLUDED — pith would be brown (reference confirms this)
- **Charcoal Rot**: Less likely — would show gray exterior + visible black microsclerotia speckling on pith/roots
- **Fusarium**: Shows similar white pith + dark roots, but Fusarium description says "brown vascular tissue" 
- **Sudden Death Syndrome**: White pith is the **key distinguishing feature** per description; dark rotted taproot also matches; SDS reference bottom-left shows similar rotted dark root system

The **white pith** is the critical diagnostic feature. The SDS description explicitly states "white pith (distinguishing from brown stem rot which causes brown discoloration of the pith)." The severely rotted, darkened root system with the white interior pith is classic SDS presentation.

The root system is severely darkened and rotted, consistent with SDS taproot discoloration. Charcoal Rot is excluded due to absence of visible black microsclerotia speckling; Brown Stem Rot excluded by white (not brown) pith."}
